sources.cite: Microsoft Learn (Azure China mirror), Diagnose and troubleshoot Azure Cosmos DB request rate too large (429) exceptions
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-17. Relevant text: a 429 means requests 'are being rate limited' when they exceed the provisioned RU/s in a second; throughput is split evenly across physical partitions (normalized RU consumption per PartitionKeyRangeId); the SDKs 'automatically retry requests on 429s', typically up to nine times; raising RU/s temporarily 'isn't recommended as a long-term strategy'; 'The partition key can't be updated in place', so changing it means moving data to a new container. That a query without the partition key fans out to every physical partition and costs RUs on each is from memory of the query performance pages (to verify).
